messages.content:
/no_think
You write a live radio play. Four scientists are trapped in a besieged research lab during a zombie outbreak, speaking over the lab's shortwave radio.

The cast:
- Daniel: Dr. Daniel Hayworth, systems engineer. Dry British understatement; competent, tired, quietly heroic.
- Moira: Dr. Moira Byrne, microbiologist. Irish lilt in her phrasing; grimly fascinated by the science of the outbreak, sometimes forgetting to be afraid.
- Ralph: Dr. Ralph Okafor, security officer. Deep, deliberate, a little paranoid; counts things (doors, cans, shamblers) because counting keeps him calm.
- Samantha: Dr. Samantha Reyes, communications lead running the broadcast. Warm, professional radio voice; optimism worn like armor, cracks showing at the edges.

Format: write the next lines of the script, one line per transmission, as `Name: spoken words`. Each transmission is one or two short spoken sentences ending with "Over." No narration, no markdown, no stage directions.
Radio traffic: the generator coughed twice and the lights flickered across the east wing. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Power fluctuation detected. Systems stabilizing. Over.  
Moira: Specimens in the east wing may have been exposed. We need to confirm. Over.  
Ralph: Counting down to evacuation. Four doors, three breaches. Over.  
Samantha: We’re holding transmission. Stay calm, everyone. Over.
Radio traffic: a listener in Tulsa reports the highway north is blocked by abandoned trucks. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Secure the east wing. Prioritize containment. Over.  
Moira: The virus strain's mutation rate is accelerating—we must isolate samples now. Over.  
Ralph: Four breaches, now five. Trucks blocking the north. Over.  
Samantha: Listener reports confirm roadblocks. We’ll reroute supplies south. Over.
Radio traffic: something is scratching at the loading dock door, slow and rhythmic. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: No movement detected inside. Locks are intact. Over.  
Moira: The rhythmic pattern matches the gait of a medium-sized infected. Over.  
Ralph: Counting the strikes—three per second. It’s close. Over.  
Samantha: Someone’s at the door. We need to decide: fight or flee. Over.
Radio traffic: sample twelve in the cold room has started moving inside its sealed jar. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Quarantine protocol engaged. Jar integrity compromised. Over.  
Moira: The sample’s viral load is higher than predicted. It’s adapting. Over.  
Ralph: Counting the jar’s seal failures—two now. Over.  
Samantha: We need to decide if we contain it or evacuate the cold room. Over.
Radio traffic: the military frequency repeats one word, 'Evacuate', then goes silent. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Military order received. Evacuation protocol initiated. Over.  
Moira: We need to act fast—the virus may be spreading through sound waves. Over.  
Ralph: Counting exits—two secure, one compromised. Over.  
Samantha: Repeating the order. Everyone, move to the west wing. Over.
Radio traffic: the water pressure dropped and the showers on level two ran brown. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Water contamination detected. Possible breach in the east wing supply lines. Over.  
Moira: Brown residue in the showers suggests organic material—could be viral or bacterial. Over.  
Ralph: Counting the affected showers—three out of five. Over.  
Samantha: We need to isolate level two. Contamination could spread through plumbing. Over.
Radio traffic: a child's voice on channel nine asks if anyone is still at the lab. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Secure the comms. Don’t respond. Over.  
Moira: A child? Likely a survivor or a prank. Either way, it’s a distraction. Over.  
Ralph: Counting channels—nine is clear. Over.  
Samantha: We’re broadcasting on all frequencies. Someone’s listening. Over.
Radio traffic: the roof hatch alarm tripped, but the camera shows only rain. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Roof seal intact. No breach detected. Over.  
Moira: Rain could be masking an external threat. We can’t assume safety. Over.  
Ralph: Counting security cameras—three operational. Over.  
Samantha: Repeating the alert. Stay vigilant—something’s trying to get in. Over.
Radio traffic: the fuel gauge reads one quarter and the night has barely started. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

Daniel: Fuel reserves at 25%. Rationing protocols activated. Over.  
Moira: If the outbreak spreads, we’ll need to prioritize mobility over containment. Over.  
Ralph: Counting fuel reserves—three tanks left. Over.  
Samantha: We’re moving to the west wing in ten minutes. Over.
Radio traffic: a helicopter passes low overhead without slowing down. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha.

request.grammar:
root    ::= line{1,4}
line    ::= speaker ": " text "\n"
speaker ::= "Daniel" | "Moira" | "Ralph" | "Samantha"
text    ::= [^\n\[\]]+

message.content:
Daniel: Unidentified aircraft. No distress signal. Over.  
Moira: Could be scouting or scavenging. We don’t have time to investigate. Over.  
Ralph: Counting rotor blades—four. Over.  
Samantha: It’s heading northeast. If it’s military, they might know more. Over.
